loci.name: k5-robustness-vs-k2-ranking-flip
loci.one_line: Does Li/Rudner/Wilson's (ICLR 2024) ensemble-size robustness claim, read in full Appendix D.3 context, actually contradict the paper's K=2-vs-K=5 surrogate-class ranking flip -- or is L/R/W's own 'small-BO-dataset diversity' explanation a THIRD mechanism that neither our K-artifact story nor candidate C's smoothness story accounts for?
loci.rationale: The width sweep already grepped L/R/W's Fig A.7 caption verbatim ('the different ensembles perform similarly across many experiments, showing the robustness of our results to this hyperparameter') and correctly flagged that L/R/W only ablates N={5,10}, never K=2 (miss-catcher-search-log-n2-n3-n6-n9-n1-residual). But the claims file for that note (research/temp/claims-a-study-of-bayesian-neural-network-surrogates-for-bayesian-optimization-iclr-202.json) also contains an UNRESOLVED third claim the summary-level pass didn't chase: 'Deep ensembles underperform... because small BO dataset sizes (rarely exceeding 600 objective queries) prevent ensemble members from finding diverse loss-landscape basins of attraction' -- a dataset-size/diversity mechanism, distinct from both K-as-capacity-artifact (N5) and smoothness-as-causal-axis (candidate C). A depth read of L/R/W's full Appendix D.3 + Section on ensemble diversity could determine whether N2's ranking-flip is (a) genuinely novel and unexplained by L/R/W, (b) explained away by their diversity argument, or (c) actually supports N5's finite-width objection more than either N2 or C realize. This directly changes how confidently N2 can be asserted NONE FOUND and how hard N5 cuts against candidate C.

opposing_positions.position: The surrogate-class ranking FLIPS with K: at K=2 the ensemble's task-normalized marginal (0.95) exceeds the exact GP's (0.846); the field-standard K=5 is where the ensemble is weakest (0.52/0.32/0.18 at K=3/5/10). This is a genuine, unclaimed K-contingency of a cross-class ranking.

Ensemble-vs-other-surrogate rankings are ROBUST to ensemble size ('the different ensembles perform similarly... showing the robustness of our results to this hyperparameter,' Fig A.7), and where ensembles do underperform it is explained by a named, different mechanism -- small BO dataset sizes preventing diverse mode-finding -- not by K being below some capacity threshold.

suggested_searches: Li Rudner Wilson Appendix D.3 ensemble diversity basins of attraction full text
deep ensemble diversity small sample regime Bayesian optimization mode collapse
ensemble size two members Bayesian optimization surrogate comparison

loci.name: smoothness-mechanism-vs-finite-width-artifact
loci.one_line: Is the ensemble's jagged posterior mean an intrinsic surrogate-CLASS property (candidate C's causal-axis thesis) or a finite-width/under-training/low-K capacity artifact (NTK/spectral-bias objection) -- and does this determine whether candidate C survives at all?
loci.rationale: This is contradiction-graph cluster 'smoothness-mechanism-vs-finite-width-artifact' (decision_relevance: high) -- validated: the sources are real (jacot-ntk, Lee ICLR18, Rahaman ICML19, L/R/W ICLR24) and the fight is genuine, not a scope mismatch, per orchestrator-notes.md's own read ('N5 is the sharpest self-inflicted risk... cuts AGAINST C and FOR D'). The width sweep established the theory-level ingredients (NTK/GP equivalence is a theorem; spectral bias is broadly replicated) but has NOT yet closely read whether the specific widths/training regimes of the paper's deep-ensemble members fall inside the NTK/spectral-bias regime these theorems actually govern, versus a looser 'ensembles are somewhat smooth-biased' hand-wave. A depth read of Jacot/Rahaman's precise conditions (width thresholds, training-time/learning-rate regime, activation function) against the paper's actual ensemble architecture would determine whether N5's objection is a precise, citable mechanism or a suggestive analogy -- this is the single fact that most decides whether candidate C (mechanism paper) is publishable at all, or whether D (taxonomy) subsumes it.

opposing_positions.position: Prior-task smoothness match is the surrogate-class axis governing the GP-ensemble gap; smoothing the ensemble should close the gap (candidate C's thesis, M1/M2 experiments).

Jaggedness is a finite-width/capacity artifact, not a class property: infinite-width nets ARE Gaussian processes (Jacot, Lee) and finite nets are spectrally biased toward low-frequency functions (Rahaman); the paper's own K=2-beats-K=5 result is capacity/averaging evidence, and L/R/W's abstract states infinite-width BNNs are 'particularly promising, especially in high dimensions.'

suggested_searches: neural tangent kernel finite width deviation threshold practical ensemble sizes
spectral bias small networks empirical width learning rate regime
when do finite ensembles NOT approximate Gaussian process posterior

loci.name: bidirectional-smoothness-manipulation-beyond-offline-mbo

loci.rationale: The width sweep's N7 search was thorough but explicitly SCOPED to offline-MBO forward-citation trees: IGNITE's 8 citers and MS-DDEO's 23 citers were both confined to the data-driven-evolutionary-algorithm literature (per claims-ignite-*.json and claims-ms-ddeo-*.json). The redundancy audit itself names this exact gap and flags it for deeper investigation: 'Flag for step 8 corpus critic: is there a NON-offline-MBO paper that roughens a smooth model to prove a smoothness->performance causal link (e.g., in BO or kernel-method literature)?' (research/temp/redundancy-audit.md). This is the single highest-leverage unresolved search for N7/candidate C: candidates worth chasing include Fourier-feature/random-feature bandwidth papers (Tancik et al.), GP length-scale-vs-NN-frequency-bias comparison papers, and deep-kernel-learning papers that deliberately vary kernel roughness against network smoothness as a controlled pair. If found, N7 flips from NONE FOUND to FOUND and candidate C's strongest unique claim collapses; if an exhaustive sweep still comes up empty, N7's NONE FOUND verdict becomes much more defensible than the current offline-MBO-scoped search supports.

loci.name: audit-shrinks-vs-strengthens-precedent-hunt
loci.one_line: Is there ANY ML/CS reality-check or reproducibility-audit paper -- beyond the already-checked Recht (relative-only) and Bressan (non-ML) -- whose de-confounded headline effect-size NUMBER exceeds its originally published value, the way the paper's eta^2_surr grows 0.37 -> 0.405?
loci.rationale: This is contradiction-graph cluster 'audit-shrinks-vs-strengthens' (decision_relevance: high) and it is explicitly the rhetorical asset that separates candidate D from 'yet another reality-check paper' (orchestrator-notes.md: 'If N9 shape is unclaimed, D is the strongest of the three'). The width sweep already ran a genuinely thorough search (miss-catcher-search-log-n2-n3-n6-n9-n1-residual) and reached a verdict of 'NOT VERIFIABLE AS A CLEAN NONE FOUND -- genuinely mixed,' with Recht et al. as a partial (relative-slope-only) ML/CS analog and Bressan as a full-shape-but-non-ML analog. Given the stakes -- this single verdict determines whether D's differentiator claim is bulletproof or needs hedging -- it warrants one more targeted pass into adjacent literatures the current sweep did not check: meta-science/multiverse-analysis papers (Steegen et al. 'increasing transparency through multiverse analysis', Simonsohn's specification-curve analysis), and recent (2023-2026) ML fairness/robustness audits where correcting a measurement bias increased a reported disparity or effect (a structurally similar 'audit reveals the true effect was being UNDERSTATED' pattern that may exist outside the benchmarking-reality-check genre specifically).

opposing_positions.position: Auditing/de-confounding SHRINKS or vanishes the effect -- the reality-check genre norm, replicated across every ML/CS example this project catalogued (Melis, Ferrari Dacrema, Musgrave, Lucic all report shrink-direction results).

De-confounding CAN grow the effect: our result (eta^2_surr 0.367->0.405) plus partial precedents -- Recht's relative model-ranking slope steepens even as absolute accuracy drops, and Bressan (psychology, non-ML) restores/strengthens a failed replication under a stricter confound-controlled spec.

suggested_searches: measurement bias correction increased reported effect machine learning fairness audit
specification curve analysis multiverse analysis effect size larger after correction
benchmark correction revealed larger gap than originally reported deep learning
audited disparity larger than originally measured fairness machine learning

loci.rationale: N3 is the THINNEST-covered claim in the corpus (coverage-gaps.md rates it 'Adequate (2-3, pending W3)' versus 'Well-covered' for every other claim) and it is one of D's five named confounds. The miss-catcher search log (research/temp/miss-catcher-search-log-n2-n3-n6-n9-n1-residual.md) ran ~10 targeted queries on 'matched pessimism,' 'conservatism coefficient,' and 'unfair uncertainty scale' phrasing, and correctly found Ghasemipour et al. as the nearest analog (different mechanism: within-ensemble target-sharing, not cross-class sigma-scale mismatch) -- but it never searched the FOUNDATIONAL GP-UCB beta_t calibration literature (Srinivas et al. 2010 and its regret-bound descendants) or practitioner-level BoTorch/scikit-optimize documentation/issues discussing kappa tuning across surrogate types, which is the most likely place a 'beta must be recalibrated per surrogate class' caveat would already be named if it exists anywhere. This is exactly the kind of claim where the current NONE FOUND verdict could flip to FOUND on a closer, differently-scoped read -- or, if it survives, becomes a much stronger NONE FOUND with a documented exact query log.

loci.name: exact-gp-scope-of-due-feature-collapse-caveat
loci.one_line: Does DUE's 'feature collapse' caveat (an unconstrained deep-kernel GP can be 'certain even far away from training data') actually apply to the paper's surrogates -- an EXACT GP and a sparse variational GP, neither of which uses a learned neural feature extractor -- or is the sigma-irrelevant reading of N4 resting on a citation whose scope doesn't match the paper's architecture?
loci.rationale: Contradiction-graph cluster 'sigma-mediated-vs-sigma-irrelevant' (decision_relevance: high) cites DUE as evidence that 'a GP does not automatically get variance growth (needs bi-Lipschitz features)' to support the sigma-irrelevant reading. But the width-sweep's own claims file for DUE (research/temp/claims-on-feature-collapse-and-deep-kernel-learning-for-single-forward-pass-uncertainty.json) shows the mechanism is specifically about Deep Kernel Learning (a neural feature extractor feeding a GP head): verbatim, 'with no constraints, the DKL objective pushes far-away data points to be mapped to the same features as those of training-set points.' The paper's own surrogates are an EXACT GP and a sparse variational GP (SVGP) -- standard stationary-kernel GPs directly on the input space, not deep-kernel GPs with a learned feature extractor. If DUE's feature-collapse caveat structurally cannot apply to a stationary-kernel exact/sparse-variational GP (which has RBF-style distance-aware variance growth by construction, with no feature-collapse failure mode), then the width sweep may be over-applying DUE's citation to argue against the sigma-mediated mechanism, and N4's 'ingredients owned, combination unclaimed' verdict needs a scope correction before the draft cites DUE against candidate C.

opposing_positions.position: Distance-aware variance growth is real for GP-family surrogates and standard/ensemble nets lack it -- SNGP formalizes this as 'input-distance awareness' and its GP-RBF baseline variance 'increases monotonically toward 1' away from training data; this supports the GP winning because of sigma-mediated implicit trust-region behavior (N4 hypothesis-at-risk).

A GP does not automatically inherit distance-aware variance growth -- DUE shows an unconstrained deep-kernel GP is 'certain even far away from the training data' due to feature collapse, so sigma-mediated mechanisms are not automatic and the beta=0 control (gap barely moves 0.51->0.47) is consistent with sigma being largely irrelevant.

suggested_searches: exact Gaussian process stationary kernel distance-aware variance growth no feature collapse
sparse variational GP inducing points variance growth away from data
deep kernel learning versus standard GP feature collapse applicability
